activity.notes: Representative chronological point at c.1125 BCE for Sisera in the Deborah-Barak conflict tradition. The primary polity remains Hazor because Judges 4 identifies Sisera as commander for Jabin associated with Hazor. This is not a lifespan, tenure, or claim of exact campaign dating; ATLAS uses one uncertain point instead of the former 1200-1100 BCE broad era window.

sources.title: Hebrew Bible — Judges 4–5
sources.citation_text: Primary textual source for Sisera as commander of Jabin associated with Hazor and opponent of Deborah and Barak.

sources.title: Eric H. Cline, The Battles of Armageddon: Megiddo and the Jezreel Valley from the Bronze Age to the Nuclear Age
sources.citation_text: Cline's historical synthesis treats the Deborah-Barak-Sisera episode under the chronological heading 1125 BCE. ATLAS uses that date only as an uncertain representative anchor, not as an exact event date.
sources.locator: Chapter: Deborah, Barak, and Sisera, 1125 B.C.

review_context.chronology_policy: Replace a broad era window with one uncertain representative point when person-specific start/end boundaries are not defensible.
